key_insight: An evaluator-guided LLM search can discover quantum circuits that beat state-of-the-art designs on both gate count and qubit count, and even enable new reversible architectures.
engineering_relevance: This suggests AI-assisted co-design can reduce the cost of practical quantum algorithms, especially where reversibility and resource trade-offs dominate implementation constraints.
method: LLMs propose candidate quantum circuit designs.
An independent evaluator verifies correctness and scores resource use.
An evolutionary search iterates across multiple problem domains to optimize Toffoli and qubit counts.
evidence_signal: Across eight benchmark tasks spanning computation, chemistry, optimization, quantum simulation, and number theory, the method significantly improved both Toffoli and qubit counts in seven cases and produced a new modular inversion architecture in the eighth.
watch_item: The gains depend on an external evaluator and careful verification, so translation to hardware-ready implementations may still face synthesis, depth, and noise constraints.
paper_title: Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models
